questions.q: What does the final Kaggle ranking use?
why: The public part is only a sample.

questions.q: Why can the public leaderboard mislead you?
options: It uses a small, noisy part of the test
why: It is not random, but noisy.

questions.q: Scenario: the test period is the next 16 days after the training data. Your validation should be:
options: The last 16 days of the training data, with training on earlier days

questions.q: Scenario: you tried 80 variants and pick the best public score. What is the risk?
options: Selection effect: the best of many noisy scores is optimistic, and the private score may be worse
The private score will be better

questions.q: Which statement about GPU quota is true?
options: It is limited per week, so start on CPU and use GPU for neural networks
A pattern in ids or row order that predicts the target but is meaningless in real life

questions.q: What file do you write to submit?
options: A CSV in the sample_submission format
why: A notebook alone is not scored.
